title: Regional bodies: Transbay authority contracts held by City payees
question: Which firms hold contracts with both the City and a regional public body, and are any of them flagged elsewhere in this project?
finding: Only one regional body publishes a contract list that could be read: the Transbay Joint Powers Authority, with 199 awards to 170 firms since 2004. 56 of those firms are also City payees ($3.70 billion from the City in fiscal 2019 to 2026), and 19 of them carry warning signs here: Anvil Builders, Inc.; AECOM Technical Services, Inc.; Allied Universal; Allied Universal Security Services; Stantec Consulting Services Inc.; Macias, Gini & O’Connell; Civic Edge Consulting; Otis Elevator Company. None of the 57 contractors on the State Labor Commissioner's public-works debarment list matches a City vendor or a Transbay awardee by name.
how: The authority's awarded-contracts page was parsed into one row per award (contract number, description, awardee, date). Each awardee was matched to City ledger vendors on the tidied name, allowing one name to be the start of the other. City payments are fiscal 2019 to 2026. Warning signs are this project's own, matched on the ledger name. The debarment list is the State Labor Commissioner's, matched on the contractor's name.
limits: Working for both the City and a regional body is ordinary for engineering, legal and construction firms, and most signs here are leads only. The Transbay list gives no dollar amounts, so the size of the regional work is unknown. BART, the Golden Gate Bridge district, the Housing Authority, the school district, City College and the county transportation authority publish no vendor ledger that could be found; their audits and inspector-general reports on disk rarely name vendors, and were not searched for names because short firm names produce false matches. A name match can join two different firms.
